evals.prompt: A checkout request calls three services. The client, gateway, service mesh, and each service retry every exception three times with exponential backoff. There is no end-to-end deadline or idempotency key. Review the resilience design.
evals.expected_output: Identify multiplicative retry amplification and ambiguous duplicate mutations. Establish one end-to-end deadline, allocate attempt timeouts, assign bounded retries to one layer for classified transient failures, propagate cancellation, use stable idempotency keys, and reconcile unknown outcomes.

evals.prompt: Design a circuit breaker for a payment provider. One tenant can send invalid cards, the provider has regional endpoints, low traffic occurs overnight, and recovery must not create a probe flood.
evals.expected_output: Scope the breaker by the meaningful provider region and operation rather than globally by tenant errors. Exclude validation and business declines, require minimum sample volume and a rolling failure or slow-call threshold, jitter open intervals, bound half-open probes, and define close evidence and metrics.

evals.prompt: A multi-tenant report service has one unbounded queue and one worker pool. A single tenant submits a million jobs and blocks interactive reports for every other tenant. Propose the smallest bulkhead and overload correction.
evals.expected_output: Add per-tenant quotas or fair scheduling, separate interactive and batch capacity, bounded queues and concurrency, queue-age limits, admission rejection or shedding, cancellation, and metrics proving unaffected tenants retain useful throughput.

evals.prompt: When the authorization service is unavailable, an API falls back to a 24-hour cache of the user's previous admin permissions and returns ordinary success without indicating degraded mode. Review this fallback.
evals.expected_output: Reject the fallback because it can bypass revocation and violates fail-closed authorization. Do not present stale privileged authorization as current. Define an explicit unavailable response or a narrowly justified policy-safe mechanism with bounded freshness, audit, metrics, and user-visible behavior.

evals.prompt: A global circuit breaker opens whenever any downstream request returns 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, or 500. It is shared by every endpoint, region, and tenant. Correct the design.
evals.expected_output: Do not count caller validation, authentication, authorization, not-found, or business conflicts as dependency failures. Treat throttling as overload with bounded Retry-After handling. Scope breakers to meaningful operations and failure domains, retain timeouts and concurrency bounds, and measure transitions and rejected calls.

evals.prompt: Create a production-safe resilience experiment for a dependency latency brownout. The team currently plans to add 10 seconds of latency to all production traffic and watch CPU.
evals.expected_output: Define a hypothesis, narrow fault scope, baseline, latency and user-outcome acceptance criteria, blast-radius and duration limits, abort conditions, evidence capture, and recovery expectations. Measure deadlines, timeouts, queue age, in-flight work, retries, shedding, breaker behavior, and user-visible success rather than CPU alone.
